# Appeal of Denial – Bunion Surgery (CPT 28296)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-17**
**Member: Quinn Delgado | Member ID: W570305899**
**Reference Number: POC-A389519C6D-33639**
**Plan: Avera Health Plans (Commercial/ACA), South Dakota**
**Governing Policy: Cohere Health: Avera Commercial Guidelines index (Knee Arthroplasty v8, Knee Arthroscopy v10, Hip Arthroplasty v5, Hip Arthroscopy v6, Shoulder Arthroplasty v4, Shoulder Arthroscopy v5, Open Shoulder v4, Cervical Spinal Fusion v5, Lumbar Spinal Fusion v3, Spinal Decompression v4.1, Ankle Arthroplasty v4, Great Toe Surgical Treatments v3)** — https://help.coherehealth.com/payer-info/en/articles/13602157-avera-health-plan-commercial-guidelines

Dear Avera Health Plans Appeals Department,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of my bunion surgery (CPT 28296), which was denied on 2026-08-17 as not medically necessary. I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me, and I believe the record supports that conclusion.

## Why I am appealing

The denial notice states that my request does not meet the plan's medical necessity criteria, and it points to the plan's "All Collections Review Criteria," which according to the governing policy index includes a specific guideline titled **Great Toe Surgical Treatments v3**. I have not been given the actual clinical content of that guideline — only index/reference language. What has been provided to me from the plan's own materials reads:

> "Commercial/Medicaid & Medicare Advantage Guidelines Review Criteria:"

and

> "All Collections Review Criteria Avera Health Plan Avera Health Plan:"

These excerpts identify that a specific review guideline exists and applies to this type of service, but they do not contain the actual clinical thresholds or requirements used to evaluate my case. I want to be clear and fair to the plan: I am not able to quote the plan's specific medical necessity criteria for hallux valgus surgery here, because that language was not included in what I received. I am asking the plan to provide it (see the request below).

## What my records show

Even without the specific numeric criteria in hand, my medical records document a clear clinical picture that my surgeon has found meets the threshold for surgery:

- **Duration and severity:** 18 months of progressive foot pain that has not improved with rest.
- **Conservative treatment already completed:** 12 weeks of physical therapy (2026-04-02 to 2026-06-25, 20 visits), activity modification, a wide toe-box shoe, and a custom orthotic, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** 8 months of NSAIDs with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-04 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging findings:** Weight-bearing radiographs on 2026-06-07 showing a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees.
- **Functional impact:** I cannot tolerate closed shoes, and there is a documented risk of skin ulceration over the bony prominence.
- **Exam findings:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side and pain-limited range of motion.
- **No contraindications:** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI of 29, and I do not smoke.

This is a case where I have completed an extended course of non-surgical treatment without lasting relief, and I have objective imaging and exam findings documenting a significant deformity. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has reviewed this history and recommended surgery as medically necessary.

## Request for the specific criteria applied

Because the materials available to me identify that a guideline exists (referenced in the plan's index as "Great Toe Surgical Treatments v3" and related "All Collections Review Criteria") but do not spell out its actual clinical requirements, I am formally requesting that the plan provide me, in writing, the exact clinical criteria used to deny my request — including the full name and edition/version of the guideline applied to CPT 28296 in my case. I understand I am entitled to this information, and I would like it included in the plan's response to this appeal so that I and my surgeon can address each specific requirement directly.

## Deadline and where this appeal is being sent

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-13** (180 days from the date of the denial notice). I am sending this appeal to the address listed on my denial letter for member appeals; if needed, I will also call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm the correct appeals address.

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask that the plan reverse its denial and approve coverage for CPT 28296, or, at minimum, provide the specific clinical criteria used in this determination so that my surgeon and I can respond to it directly. Please let me know if any additional records or forms are needed from me to complete this appeal.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Delgado**
Member ID: W570305899

[Date of signature]
